issues.legal_issue: A merely incorrect occupancy entry in the specified revenue records does not cease to determine entitlement to possession unless it is fictitious, fraudulent, surreptitious, or maliciously introduced.
material_facts: A claimant relied on an entry recording him as occupant of the plots in the relevant revenue records to seek possession and claim adhivasi status.
The opposing party said he had redeemed a mortgage and remained in possession, and the Additional Commissioner treated the occupancy entry as fictitious based merely on that possession.
There was no evidence that the entry was fictitious, fraudulent, surreptitious, or introduced out of ill-will or hostility.
issues.conclusion: The entry, though potentially incorrect, was not shown to be fictitious or otherwise non-genuine and therefore governed the determination of entitlement to possession and adhivasi status. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20(b)(i) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, makes the specified Khasra or Khatauni entry the basis for determining who may take or retain possession. The entry must be disregarded if fictitious or made fraudulently or surreptitiously; mere incorrectness does not make it a nullity. Bachan v. Kankar explains that an incorrect entry introduced through ill-will or hostility cannot confer rights, and Vishwa Vijai Bharti v. Fakhrul Hasan clarifies that the presumption of correctness applies to genuine entries, which may be challenged as fraudulent or forged but not merely for being incorrect.

predicates.adhivasi_possession_entitlement_dispute: The proceeding concerns who is entitled to take or retain possession of land on a claim to adhivasi status.
predicates.qualifying_occupancy_entry_exists: A revenue record of the relevant kind and period records a person as occupant of the land.
predicates.entry_is_fictitious_fraudulent_sur­repti: The occupancy entry was fabricated, fraudulently or surreptitiously made, or introduced because of ill-will or hostility.
predicates.qualifying_occupancy_entry_governs_posse: The qualifying occupancy entry determines who is entitled to take or retain possession of the land.

issues.definition: In an adhivasi possession-entitlement dispute, if a qualifying occupancy entry exists and was not made fictitiously, fraudulently, surreptitiously, or out of hostility, that entry governs possession entitlement.
